newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: ADB to loan Cambodia more than $36 million.
newsitem.headline: ADB to loan Cambodia more than $36 million.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has agreed to loan Cambodia $20 million for water supply improvements and will provide another $16.8 million for airport renovations by the end of the year, a government finance official said on Tuesday.

The loans bring the ADB's total lending to Cambodia to a record $105 million for 1996 and make the ADB the country's largest multilateral source of loans, according to a Ministry of Finance statement.

Secretary of State for Finance Sun Chanthol said ADB President Mitsuo Sato and Finance Minister Keat Chhon signed the $20 million loan agreement for a Phnom Penh municipal water and drainage supply system in meetings in Manila on Monday.

On Tuesday, ADB officials were to discuss a $16.8 million loan co-financed by the ADB and the Japanese government for airport renovations in Siem Reap, the northern town that is home to the Angkor Wat temples, government officials said.
A loan agreement for the airport project will be signed by late December, Sun Chanthol said.
In 1996, the ADB has also provided funds for agriculture, health and education projects, according to the Ministry of Finance statement.
Since 1992, the ADB's cumulative lending to Cambodia totals $230 million, the statement said.
